name: @pipeworx/mcp-polymarket-us

tools.name: polymarket_us_search
tools.description: Market search/discovery on Polymarket US (polymarket.us) — the SEPARATE, CFTC-regulated, US-licensed venue, distinct from the offshore `polymarket` pack and from `kalshi`. Pass `query` for a keyword search across the full market corpus (returns matching events, each with its child markets and live prices). Omit `query` to BROWSE instead — the highest-volume open markets right now, optionally filtered by `category` (e.g. "macro", "sports", "politics"). Use for "what does Polymarket US have on X", "biggest markets trading right now on the regulated US venue", or as a first step before polymarket_us_bbo / polymarket_us_book / polymarket_us_price_history / polymarket_us_settlement, all of which need a market `slug` this tool returns. Every market price is YES-side implied probability in [0,1].

query.description: Keyword search, e.g. "fed rate", "election", "nfl". Omit to browse the highest-volume open markets instead.

status.description: open | closed (default open). With a query, filters the search; without one, "open" means active & not closed, "closed" means closed.

category.description: Browse-only filter, e.g. "macro", "sports", "politics", "crypto". Ignored when `query` is set (Polymarket US search has no category filter).

tools.name: polymarket_us_bbo
tools.description: Best bid/offer (lightweight top-of-book) for one Polymarket US market by slug — current price, last trade price, best bid, best ask, bid/ask depth (number of price levels), open interest, shares traded, and market state. Use before quoting a price when you need just the top of book, not the full depth ladder (for that, see polymarket_us_book). Get a slug from polymarket_us_search.

slug.description: Polymarket US market slug (e.g. "aec-nfl-lac-ten-2025-11-02"), from polymarket_us_search.

tools.name: polymarket_us_book
tools.description: Full order book (bid/ask depth ladder with size at every visible price level) plus session stats — open/high/low/last-trade price, shares traded, notional traded, open interest — for one Polymarket US market by slug. Use to check actual tradable depth before sizing a trade; polymarket_us_bbo gives only the top of book. Get a slug from polymarket_us_search.

slug.description: Polymarket US market slug, from polymarket_us_search.

tools.name: polymarket_us_price_history
tools.description: Historical Yes/No display-price time series for one Polymarket US market by slug. `interval` picks a fixed lookback window (1h | 6h | 1d | 1w | 1m | all); `fidelity` is the spacing between points in minutes (default 60). Returns an array of {timestamp, yes_price, no_price} — these are DISPLAY prices (yes normally derived from the best ask, no from one minus the best bid) and preserve the bid/ask spread, so yes_price + no_price can exceed 1.0 — that is not a data error. Get a slug from polymarket_us_search.

slug.description: Polymarket US market slug, from polymarket_us_search.

tools.name: polymarket_us_settlement
tools.description: Settlement (resolution) result for one Polymarket US market by slug — the final settlement price, which is 1 for the winning side / 0 for the losing side on a binary market (and can be a fractional value for a 50/50 or partial settlement). Three distinguishable outcomes: a settled market returns `settled: true` with the price; an open market that exists but has not resolved returns `settled: false` with no price and a "still open" message; a slug that does not exist on Polymarket US returns `error: "not_found"` with `settled: null` — it is NEVER reported as "still open". Use after polymarket_us_search / a known slug to check how a market actually resolved. NOTE: this tool returns a price only, no settlement timestamp — Polymarket US does not publish one on this endpoint.

slug.description: Polymarket US market slug, from polymarket_us_search.

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-polymarket-us forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the polymarket-us pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
